title: Compatible equivariant injective resolution and homogeneous injective total target
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on a small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], and let $G$ be a profinite group, with $\underline G(S)=C(S,G)$. Let $\mathcal E$ be internal $G$-equivariant $A$-modules, $\mathcal M$ internal $A$-modules, $U:\mathcal E\to\mathcal M$ the forgetful functor, and $F=\Gamma_G$ invariants [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Use ordinary cochain derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

For every profinite parameter $P$, the free internal module $A[\underline P]$ is the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{V\to P}A(V)$, equivalently extension by zero of $A|_P$ along the slice projection, and is flat (tensoring with it is exact). The translation-action functor $L(M)=A[\underline G]\otimes_A M$ is an exact left adjoint of $U$; the adjunction sends $h:M\to UJ$ to $[g]\otimes m\mapsto g\cdot h(m)$, with inverse evaluation at $[1]$. The functor $U$ is exact and preserves injectives.

For every equivariant module $N$, there exists a nonnegative equivariant injective resolution $s:N[0]\to I^\bullet$; for every such resolution $Us$ is an injective resolution in $\mathcal M$, and $I$ is K-injective (every map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null-homotopic). Form the first-quadrant double complex
$$T^{p,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^{p+1}],UI^q),\qquad p,q\geq0,$$
using the underived internal Hom and free modules of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data, def-sfb-condensed-homogeneous-functions]. Its action is $(g\cdot f)(h_0,\ldots,h_p)=g\cdot_{I^q}f(g^{-1}h_0,\ldots,g^{-1}h_p)$, its horizontal differential is the alternating sum of coordinate deletions, and its vertical differential is postcomposition with $d_I$. These differentials commute and are equivariant. The finite-diagonal total $T$ has $T^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}T^{p,q}$ and differential $d_h+(-1)^p d_I$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Every $T^{p,q}$ and every $T^n$ is equivariantly injective, and $T$ vanishes below zero. Constants in bidegree $(0,q)$ define an equivariant cochain map $\delta:I\to T$. All action and adjunction formulas hold after every profinite base change.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor] on the coherent profinite site with finite jointly surjective covers, with the represented condensed set $\underline P$: under the section-module equivalence, $A[\underline P]$ is the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{V\to P}A(V)$. This is precisely the module $j_{P!}A_P$ described in [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat]. Its flatness follows from that node, with $\mathcal C$ the chosen small coherent profinite site, $\mathcal O$ the section-ring sheaf of $A$, and $U=P$. The exact tensor comparison and reflection of flatness in [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] transfer this conclusion to internal $A$-modules. Thus $A[\underline P]\otimes_A-$ is exact for every allowed profinite $P$, including $G$ and all its finite powers.

source.place: Tag 03EV, label lemma-j-shriek-flat, clause (2) and displayed direct-sum formula; internal transfer is the cited tensor-comparison node.

proof.text: Construct $L(M)=A[\underline G]\otimes_A M$ with $k([g]\otimes m)=[kg]\otimes m$. Use the canonical generalized generators of the fixed free adjunction in the current linearization statement. Its free-generator universal property of [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor] and the tensor universal property of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] extend this formula to the sheaf tensor, so it is not an assertion of sectionwise freeness after sheafification. For variable $k$ use its restriction on every slice $T\to S$; multiplication in $G$ commutes with restriction. The identities $1g=g$ and $k(lg)=(kl)g$ give the action laws of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. A linear map $h:M\to UJ$ gives $\widetilde h([g]\otimes m)=g h(m)$; this is balanced, natural on every slice and equivariant since $\widetilde h([kg]\otimes m)=k\widetilde h([g]\otimes m)$. Conversely an equivariant $b:L(M)\to J$ gives $h(m)=b([1]\otimes m)$. Then $b([g]\otimes m)=g b([1]\otimes m)$ shows the two operations are inverse, and pre- and postcomposition commute with the formulas. They give the stated natural adjunction $L\dashv U$.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure], the action and underlying module categories are abelian, and forgetting creates sectionwise kernels and sheafified sectionwise cokernels and detects exactness. Hence $U$ is exact. The underlying functor of $L$ is the exact tensor functor of Step 1 with $P=G$; detection of exactness by $U$ makes $L$ exact in the action category. Apply [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] to this exact additive $L$ and its right adjoint $U$ from Step 2: $U$ preserves injectives. No inference from exactness of $U$ alone is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written resolution normalization helper; internal induction and homogeneous double-complex construction.

proof.text: The action category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure], so [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] gives enough injectives. Explicitly set $C^0=N$, choose monomorphisms $i_q:C^q\hookrightarrow I^q$ into injectives, put $C^{q+1}=\operatorname{coker}i_q$ with quotient $\pi_q:I^q\to C^{q+1}$, and set $d_I^q=i_{q+1}\pi_q$. These choices exist recursively by enough injectives. Since $\pi_{q+1}i_{q+1}=0$, $d_I^{q+1}d_I^q=0$; monicity of $i_{q+1}$ and epimorphicity of $\pi_{q-1}$ give $\ker d_I^q=\operatorname{im}i_q=\operatorname{im}d_I^{q-1}$ for $q>0$ and $\ker d_I^0=i_0(N)$. Extend by zero below zero: this is the desired resolution in the sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For ANY such nonnegative injective resolution, Step 3 makes every $UI^q$ injective and makes $Us$ a quasi-isomorphism, hence an underlying injective resolution. The general bounded-below-injectives theorem [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] applies in the abelian action category with lower bound zero and gives that $I$ is K-injective.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written resolution normalization helper; internal induction and homogeneous double-complex construction.

proof.text: For each $q\geq0$, Step 3 gives injectivity of $UI^q$. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-homogeneous-functions-injective] with $J=I^q$ and $n=p$. It supplies the internal homogeneous function object $T^{p,q}$ with exactly the displayed diagonal action and proves that it is equivariantly injective. Its hypothesis is underlying injectivity, now verified, and it allows arbitrary profinite $G$ and arbitrary commutative condensed $A$. All evaluations and its action are internal, after every profinite base change.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written resolution normalization helper; internal induction and homogeneous double-complex construction.

proof.text: Define $D_i:T^{p,q}\to T^{p+1,q}$ by precomposition with deletion of coordinate $i$, using the canonical generator-preserving functorial free maps of [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor], and set $d_h=\sum_{i=0}^{p+1}(-1)^iD_i$. Set $d_v(f)=d_I^q\circ f$. These are maps of the actual slice Homs of [def-sfb-condensed-homogeneous-functions]. Deleting a coordinate commutes with simultaneous left translation, so each $D_i$ is equivariant for their stated action; equivariance of $d_I^q$ gives the same for $d_v$. In $d_h^2$, deleting positions $i<j$ occurs twice: delete $j$ then $i$ with sign $(-1)^{i+j}$, or delete $i$ then position $j-1$ with sign $(-1)^{i+j-1}$. The terms cancel, so $d_h^2=0$. Also $d_v^2=0$, and postcomposition with $d_I$ commutes with every precomposition $D_i$, giving $d_hd_v=d_vd_h$. The formulas are natural under restriction of the test object, so these are equalities of internal equivariant maps.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written resolution normalization helper; internal induction and homogeneous double-complex construction.

proof.text: Totalize by [def-sp-double-complex-total]. On the $(p,q)$ summand the differential is $d_h+(-1)^pd_v$; its mixed terms are $(-1)^{p+1}d_vd_h$ and $(-1)^pd_hd_v$, which cancel by Step 6. In degree $n\geq0$ there are just $n+1$ summands, all injective by Step 5. To check their biproduct is injective, let $X\hookrightarrow Y$ be monic and $a:X\to\bigoplus_{p+q=n}T^{p,q}$. Project $a$ to each summand, extend each component to $Y$ by [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and combine the finitely many extensions using the biproduct projections and inclusions. The resulting map extends $a$. Thus $T^n$ is injective. For $n<0$ the sum is empty, so $T^n=0$ (also injective).

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written resolution normalization helper; internal induction and homogeneous double-complex construction.

proof.text: Define $c_q:I^q\to T^{0,q}$ by $c_q(m)(h)=m$ on every profinite slice, with $m$ restricted to that slice. Free linear extension followed by the tensor--Hom adjunction [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] makes this an internal linear map. The action formula of [def-sfb-condensed-homogeneous-functions] gives $(g\cdot c_q(m))(h)=g m=c_q(gm)(h)$, so it is equivariant. Its horizontal differential is $c_q(m)(h_1)-c_q(m)(h_0)=0$, and $d_vc_q(m)(h)=d_I(m)=c_{q+1}(d_I m)(h)$. Therefore its coprojection to the $(0,q)$ summand of the total of [def-sp-double-complex-total] defines $\delta:I\to T$ with $d_T\delta=\delta d_I$: the vertical sign there is $(-1)^0=1$. Every formula in this construction, including those of Step 2, uses only restricted sections, continuous multiplication or inversion, the internal action and internal linear maps; these commute with every profinite base change. This proves the required normalization of all formulas.
